dc-outstanding-yoy.direction: YoY growth decelerated from 2.65% in Jun 2026 to 2.03% in Jul 2026 — a 0.62pp decline. The rate is at the minimum of the 19-period distribution (below the 25th percentile at 2.7%).
chain: Debit cards outstanding grew 2.03% year-on-year, down 0.62pp from 2.65% prior period.
The 2.03% rate is the lowest in the 19-period series, below the 25th percentile at 2.7%.
The 0.62pp decline is the sharpest single-month deceleration since the Apr 2026 purge.
This confirms the market has not stabilised at a new equilibrium.
dc-outstanding-yoy.inference: Debit card growth is decelerating again after two months of stability — the 2.03% YoY rate is down 0.62pp from 2.65% prior period, confirming the market has not stabilised at a new equilibrium. The 2.03% rate is the lowest in 19 months, signaling the market is in the lower range of its historical growth trajectory. The Apr 2026 deceleration from 5.4% to 2.8% was the sharpest in this dataset, and the Jul 2026 decline to 2.03% confirms the market is still slowing.

dc-psb-share.title: PSB debit share at 63.68% — erosion continues for third month
dc-psb-share.observation: Public sector banks' share of debit cards outstanding stands at 63.68% in Jul 2026, down 0.11pp from 63.79% in Jun 2026.
dc-psb-share.direction: Share fell from 63.79% in Jun 2026 to 63.68% in Jul 2026 — a 0.11pp decline. The three-month trajectory since the Apr 2026 peak: 64.17% → 63.97% → 63.79% → 63.68%, a cumulative 0.49pp erosion.
chain: PSB debit share fell 0.11pp to 63.68% in Jul 2026, the third consecutive monthly decline since the Apr 2026 peak of 64.17%.
The cumulative three-month erosion of 0.49pp has now erased the entire Apr 2026 surge, which had briefly reversed a 14-month slide.
The 63.68% level is below the historical median (p25=63.4%, p75=64.6%), confirming the Apr 2026 rebalancing was temporary and the structural erosion trend has resumed.
dc-psb-share.inference: The Apr 2026 purge-driven surge has fully unwound — PSB debit share has now fallen for three straight months, eroding 0.49pp to 63.68%, below the historical median. The erosion pace (0.16pp per month on average) matches the pre-purge trend, confirming private banks and fintechs are again gaining ground in debit card issuance.
